purpose: Three isolated shot-002 tests. Same locked-camera motion and distant-world instructions; compare line display, junction dots and rotating junction dots. Single first frame avoids conflicting endpoint background cues. Current shotlist/animatic unchanged.
promptLock: PROMPT LOCK: Cinematic painterly graphic-novel space adventure, detailed but coherent with the approved illustration. Harper is an adult freckled woman with curly auburn hair, gray short-sleeve tee, gray trousers and bare feet. Her ship is a clear spherical cabin, dark satin gray metal equatorial band and upper/lower circular platforms, continuous warm amber rim lights, sparse cyan rectangular lights and one aft vertical engine ring with a cyan inner arc. Moon A is larger charcoal volcanic basalt with orange fissures; Moon B is smaller pale cyan ice with blue fractures. All celestial bodies share an offscreen upper-right sun; lava may self-emit. No extra moons, no text, no logos, no HUD. Broad focus and consistent ship geometry. Shell appearance: ultra-thin transparent technological field with a faint cyan spherical geodesic display; no thick shiny glass, lens distortion or broad refractive streaks. Interior views have no visible glass perimeter; exterior silhouette uses only subtle field glow. Metal bands and platforms keep their full geometry.

shots.prompt:
Single continuous interior shot. Camera LOCKED: no pan, tilt, zoom, orbit or dolly. Only Harper gently floats leftward from her partly cropped starting position toward a settled close portrait; hands and arms below frame, subtle hair drift and breathing, no speech. Keep first 0.5 second calm, settle near 6.167 seconds and retain a quiet lead-out through 7 seconds. DEPTH: planet, moons, nebula and stars form the distant astronomical environment. Both enormous moons are far beyond the visible planet surface, vastly larger and farther away than the six-metre cabin. No orbital motion is visible over seven seconds. Keep their apparent diameters constant and their positions fixed relative to neighboring stars. Planet limb and stars stay fixed too. Cabin ring and field are local foreground structures; they never drag the moons or background with them. Do not make moons into small balls, cabin accessories, reflections or nearby satellites. They are not attached to the field. No moving moons, growing moons, glass distortion, camera shake, cut or morph. Retain the original faint hexagonal field lines, static relative to the metal ship. The display does not rotate.
